2019_134_052119regmtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for the Troy Board of Education regular meeting of May 21, 2019 at the Services Building. It carries the March 2019 Treasurer's Report, with total disbursements in period of $9,313,671.57 and a General Fund balance of $28,656,777 at March 31, four administrative appointments effective July 1, 2019 — William Turner as Director of College & Career Programming, Kristin Martin and Michael Munaco as assistant principals at Athens, and Christine DiPilato as Assistant Superintendent for Secondary Instruction — a $631,107.36 high school science materials adoption, and five business items including a Chartwells food service agreement and $949,000.00 of trim and door frames for the new preschool.

**Meeting**
Regular meeting, May 21, 2019, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois.

**Recognition**
Five items: a Mission Moment on the Wass Wolves' Wellness Night sponsored by the Wass PTO in January; the TSD Athletics Coach-Athlete-Parent Pact; the Outstanding Support Staff Person of the Year; the district's retirees; and Teacher Appreciation Week.

**Consent agenda**
Minutes of the April 9 workshop and April 16 meeting, the March 2019 Treasurer's Report, approval of the Oakland Intermediate School District budget, and a resolution to hold a public hearing on the proposed 2019/2020 budget.

**Treasurer's Report — March 2019**
Check disbursements total $6,900,495.55 — General Fund $4,663,198.13, Special Revenue Funds $173,726.44, Other Funds $2,063,570.98 — with ACH debits of $62,035.90, outgoing wire transfers of $2,105,246.27, P-Card purchases of $251,401.05 and prior period voids of ($5,507.20), giving total disbursements in period of $9,313,671.57. Capital Projects Funds account for 1,911,445.42 of the check total and Special Education 225,387.24.

| Fund, July 1 2018 – March 31 2019 | Revenue collected | Fund balance, March 31, 2019 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| General Fund (101, 120, 122) | $100,998,819 of $153,199,134 | $28,656,777 |
| Debt Service (312, 314, 315, 316) | $16,008,828 of $16,000,000 | $15,126,662 |
| Special Revenue (520, 529, 530, 531, 535) | $7,189,272 of $10,535,267 | $2,851,019 |
| Food Service (520) | $2,438,269 of $3,397,117 | $1,042,786 |
| Troy Career Center (529) | $1,168,111 of $2,445,150 | ($365,486) |
| Adult & Community Education (530) | $3,499,400 of $4,135,000 | $1,526,660 |
| Troy Preschool (531) | $12,946 of $423,000 | ($197,695) |
| Facilities Rental (535) | $70,546 of $135,000 | $844,754 |

General Fund expenditures stand at $97,584,514 of a $155,009,522 budget, 62.95 percent, leaving $57,425,009. State sources are the laggard on the revenue side at 55.32 percent collected and federal sources at 20.05 percent, against local sources at 97.86 percent. The Debt Service fund shows principal redemption of $10,565,000 not yet paid and half the interest disbursed, which is why its balance sits at $15,126,662 mid-year.

**Personnel — four appointments, all effective July 1, 2019**
William Turner becomes Director of College & Career Programming after a 19-year career: teacher at Utica High School, counselor at Jeannette Junior High and Stevenson High School in Sterling Heights, then counselor at Troy High, night supervisor for Adult Education and principal for Summer School, and the last seven years as Assistant Principal at Athens. Kristin Martin and Michael Munaco become assistant principals at Athens, she from Clarkston Junior High and Clarkston High School where she was also a behavioral interventionist and restorative practice coordinator, he currently Career Focused Education Department Chair at Seaholm. Christine DiPilato becomes Assistant Superintendent for Secondary Instruction on a 17-year career. Each is a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure.

**Curriculum and business**
A report on high school science materials is followed by adoption of the recommended materials for grades 9-12 in the amount of $631,107.36 for the 2019-20 school year. The five business items are: authorization to finalize a Chartwells food service agreement for 2019/20 with options to renew through 2023/24, contingent on Michigan Department of Education approval, after bids opened April 18, 2019 from Aramark, Chartwells and Sodexo; playground loose fill surfacing material for all 12 elementary schools and the preschool playground at Athens High School awarded to Rolar Property Services, Inc. at $145,603.00 from the Capital Maintenance Fund; preschool technology — projectors, paging and classroom audio systems, reviewed by Director of Technology Beth Soggs with Convergent Technology Partners — at $117,601.85 from the Early Childhood Center Fund; flooring replacement bid alternates to Conventional Carpet at $94,883.00; and Troy Preschool trim and door frames to Barton Malow at not more than $949,000.00 from the Early Childhood Capital Projects Fund.

**Other**
Two resolutions close the agenda. The first commemorates the ratification of the 19th Amendment at the request of the Oakland County Board of Commissioners: districts submitting resolutions receive a 19th Amendment Suffragette Victory Flag to be flown June 10-14, 2019 for the centennial of Michigan's ratification, and again countywide from August 24-28, 2020 for the centennial of federal ratification. The second supports proper funding of education in Michigan.

Agenda packet for the regular meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, May 21, 2019, 7:00 PM at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. The agenda is: 1. Pledge of Allegiance; 2. Recognition — A. TSD Mission Moment: Wass Wolves Wellness Program, B. TSD Athletics CAP Pact, C. Outstanding Support Staff Person of the Year, D. Troy School District Retirees, E. Teacher Appreciation Week; 3. Additions & Deletions; 4. Public Communication (agenda items); 5. General – Consent Agenda; 6. Personnel; 7. Curriculum; 8. Business; 9. Public Communication (non-agenda items); 10. Other; 11. Adjournment.

**Recognition.** The Mission Moment recognizes Wass Elementary School, where the Wass PTO sponsored the Wass Wolves' Wellness Night in January. Wass holds a learning night for its students every year, with recent years focusing on science, literacy, math and visual arts. The remaining recognition items are the TSD Athletics CAP Pact, the Outstanding Support Staff Person of the Year, the district's retirees, and Teacher Appreciation Week.

**Consent agenda.** A. Minutes of the April 9, 2019 Board of Education Workshop. B. Minutes of the April 16, 2019 Board of Education Meeting. C. Treasurer's Report for March 2019. D. Approve Oakland Intermediate School District Budget. E. Resolution to Hold a Public Hearing on the Proposed 2019/2020 School Year Budget.

**Personnel: four administrative appointments.** Each resolution issues a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure.

Item 6.A recommends Mr. William Turner as Director, College & Career Programming, beginning July 1, 2019. His 19-year career began as a teacher at Utica High School; he then served as a counselor at Jeannette Junior High School and Stevenson High School, both in Sterling Heights, before joining Troy as a counselor at Troy High School. He has also been Night Supervisor for the district's Adult Education Department and Principal for Troy School District Summer School, and has spent the last seven years as Assistant Principal at Athens High School. He served as a district team member for the New Pedagogies for Deep Learning Cohort, headed the District Vision Team for Career and Technical Education, and mentored five teacher leaders aspiring to administration. He holds a Bachelor of Science in English from Michigan State University, a Master of Arts in School Counseling from Sienna Heights College and an Education Specialist Degree in Education Leadership from Saginaw Valley University.

Item 6.B recommends Ms. Kristin Martin as Assistant Principal, Athens High School. She began as a Social Studies Teacher at Brandon High School in Ortonville and is presently a Social Studies Teacher at Clarkston Junior High and Clarkston High School, having also served as a Behavioral Interventionist at Clarkston High School and Restorative Practice Coordinator at Clarkston Junior High School. She has been part of a Trauma-Informed Champions Learning Group, a Teaching and Learning Council member, and has held various coaching positions. She holds a Bachelor of Liberal Arts and Education from the University of Detroit-Mercy, a Master in the Art of Teaching from Marygrove College, and an Educational Specialist Degree in Leadership from Oakland University.

Item 6.C recommends Mr. Michael Munaco as Assistant Principal, Athens High School. He began as a Computer Technology Teacher at Fitzgerald High School in Warren, moved to Chatterton Middle School in Warren as a History and World Languages Teacher, then became a Business Teacher at Seaholm High School in Birmingham, where he is currently Career Focused Education Department Chair. He has been involved with School Improvement and 5D+ Staff Evaluation. He holds a Bachelor of Arts in Marketing and Management from Northwood University, a Master in the Art of Teaching from Wayne State University, and an Educational Specialist Degree in Leadership with Administrator Certificate from Oakland University.

Item 6.D recommends Ms. Christine DiPilato as Assistant Superintendent, Secondary Instruction, on a distinguished 17-year career in education.

**Curriculum.** Item 7.A is a report on recommended high school science materials; item 7.B adopts them, resolving that the recommended science materials for grades 9-12 in the amount of $631,107.36 be approved for the 2019-20 school year.

**Business.** Item 8.A concerns contracted food service. Bids were opened on April 18, 2019 for Food Service Management, submitted by Aramark, Chartwells and Sodexo. The resolution authorizes Administration to proceed with finalizing an agreement with Chartwells to provide food services for the 2019/20 school year, with options to renew for 2020/21, 2021/22, 2022/23 and 2023/24, contingent upon final approval by the Michigan Department of Education, the contract to be consistent with the terms and conditions of the original Request For Proposal dated March 18, 2019 and subsequent addendums.

Item 8.B awards playground loose fill surfacing material — sought by RFP for all 12 elementary schools and the preschool playground at Athens High School, with bids reviewed by the TSD Operations Department — to Rolar Property Services, Inc. in the amount of $145,603.00 as an expenditure of the Capital Maintenance Fund.

Item 8.C awards preschool technology for the Troy School District Preschool, an RFP for projectors, paging and classroom audio systems reviewed by Beth Soggs, Director of Technology, with Convergent Technology Partners, in the amount of $117,601.85 as an expenditure of the Early Childhood Center Fund.

Item 8.D awards flooring replacement bid alternates to Conventional Carpet in the amount of $94,883.00. Item 8.E awards Troy Preschool trim and door frames to Barton Malow in an amount not to exceed $949,000.00 as an expenditure of the Early Childhood Capital Projects Fund; the attached bid material is prepared by Barton Malow Company of 1274 Library St, Detroit, with Stephanie Buhagiar as bid package lead, under project 180281, Troy School District ECC Wood Trim & Frames.

**Other.** Item 10.A is a resolution commemorating the ratification of the 19th Amendment. The Oakland County Board of Commissioners asked school boards to help commemorate the passage of the amendment guaranteeing and protecting women's constitutional right to vote; districts submitting resolutions receive a 19th Amendment Suffragette Victory Flag to be flown June 10-14, 2019 in honor of the 100th anniversary of Michigan's ratification, with the flags flown again countywide from August 24-28, 2020 in honor of the 100th anniversary of federal ratification. The resolution recites that women of every race, class and ethnic background across America have made historic contributions to the growth and strength of the United States in countless recorded and unrecorded ways, and that the women of this nation initiated the most significant women's movement in history. Item 10.B is a resolution in support of proper funding of education in Michigan.
